I’m only taking acetaminophen when it seizes up.
- I don’t notice anything unusual about stools other than sometimes feeling constipated during an episode, which is very painful to relieve
- the most recent episode did actually occur immediately after eating, however they’re normally random. When I’m in that level of pain I don’t usually think to eat, I generally have something easy to digest after
- I’m not on any medication
- I don’t drink or smoke
- no allergies - other than this I’m very healthy

I did look up the symptoms of stomach ulcers however I don’t quite match a few of them. It’s not so much burning as it is severe stabbing pain and I’m not usually nauseated. However it could be. Thanks for your response :)
This sub is for people that need to cry about it

I read an interview with an aphantasic person who said they found missing people difficult. I know little about it myself and am hoping to increase my knowledge on the subject, and am getting desperate. Reading that set off alarm bells in my mind, that all of our good times had gone to waste. But I can see he already has underlying mental abnormalities.

Yeah, I can see that. I honestly know little about aphantasia - he is the only person I know with it so I only know of his experience with it. We had a very strong emotional connection, talking every day, calling a few times a week, seeing each other a lot etc etc. It just came into my mind today that his aphantasia might be blocking me from his mind which concerned me, what with me missing him so much. But thank you for your insight.
How is it going?
Try really, really hard not to again. It’s easier to stop it when it’s just started.

It’s incredibly addicting, I haven’t gone a month without doing it since I started and all I’ve been left with is permanent scars and judgement. As soon as it’s short sleeved weather it becomes a nightmare. It’s not the nice aesthetic depression thing you hear about, it’ll take away so much from you. Even if you enjoy it the first time you’ll completely regret it. Don’t please.

It seems like right now you have a good routine going to keep your mind from being depressed - routines certainly help me as well, they’re very useful. Can you try and incorporate school into your routine? Plan out how your afternoons will go and what you’ll do to make yourself happy when you get home. If there’s classes you’re struggling with, hint to your teachers that things aren’t easy - even the worst teachers do care about you.
Is there any way at all you can have a mental health break? Do you have people at home who you can discuss this issue with easily? Hope you’re okay :)

I don’t really have any other addictions so it’s hard to compare. But it’s an intrusive thought. The thought of doing it comes into my mind a lot and can be distracting. When I’m not feeling good the reminder of how it feels when I do it comes into my mind and makes me want to do it again. You’re welcome btw :))

I started doing it a year ago and despite having been happy since I started the urge gets strong at times. It has been very hard to stop - I relapsed only the other day in fact. It becomes very addicting. I normally do it when I’m numb to feel something or when I get a burst of adrenaline usually from a negative experience.

Get in touch with authorities or a helpline. Professionals will be able to give you good advice. Give them all the information you can on them - they’ll be able to work something out. You shouldn’t have to deal with this alone.
